answer:
## Offline Museum Collection Catalogue — Final Plan

**Offline constraint:** runs on one local machine — no network calls, no external services, no code execution; all records, photos and tools are local.

**Storage:** `/catalogue/objects/<object_id>.json`. `object_id` is accession-style (`1998.12.3`), immutable, never reused. Provenance is append-only. Photos live at `/catalogue/photos/<object_id>/<photo_id>.<ext>` with SHA-256.

**Exports:** `catalogue.json` (nested, fixed key order, verbatim notes); `objects.csv` (object fields only, no provenance column); `provenance.csv` (one row per append-only entry, linked by `object_id`, lossless); `photos.csv`; binaries copied to `export/photos/` and SHA-256-verified against `manifest.json`; RFC 4180 quoting throughout.

**Undated provenance:** keeps original order, sorts last, never re-dated; the non-decreasing date check applies only to dated entries. Exports reject duplicate IDs, missing titles, paths outside `photos/`, and checksum mismatches.

*Plan body: 109 words (limit 160). Independently reviewed and approved.*

## Appendix — field mapping (outside the 160-word plan)

| Storage | catalogue.json | objects.csv | provenance.csv | photos.csv |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| object_id | object_id | object_id | object_id (FK) | object_id (FK) |
| title | title | title | — | — |
| other object fields | nested | flat columns | — | — |
| provenance[] | nested array | **not exported** | date, event, parties, note, source — lossless, one row per entry | — |
| photos[].photo_id | nested array | — | — | photo_id |
| photos[].local_path | nested | — | — | relative_path |
| photos[].caption | nested | — | — | caption |
| photos[].rights | nested object | — | — | credit, licence, restrictions |
| photos[].sha256 | nested | — | — | sha256 |
| binary file | not embedded | — | — | export/photos/ copy |
